main_text.l: Similiter & graue quippiam potētia graue est,
& conatur actu quidem quoque tale fieri, id est, re
ipsa deorsum descendere: sed quoniam sorte imposi-
tum est excelsæ columnæ, aut simili rei, impeditur,
nec potest prius deorsum tendere, quàm columna
& omne impedimentum per aliquem remoueatur.
Iam ex his licet colligere, quòd leuia sursum, grauia
deorsum tendant, duabus id de causis euenire.
1. Quòd à primo generationis suæ tempore acce-
pe-rint formam, secundum quam apta nata sunt, na-
turaliter sursum uel deorsum ferri.
2. Quòd adiuuentur ab eo quod remouet impe-
dimentum, per quod prohibebantur, ne actu ferent
huiusmodi. Prima causa est per se mouens, posterior
per accidens. Itaq; mouentur quidem illa sic natu-
raliter, quandoquidem habent principium motus
in seipsis, non tamen habent principium mouendi:
hoc est, habent principium passiuum, at non acti-
uum. Quòd enim moueantur, quò per naturam te-
ndunt, acceptum ferri ei debet, à quo remouetur im-
pedimenta. Ergo grauia & leuia non mouetur à se
ipsis, sed præcipuè à remouente impedimentum.
Probatum igitur abundè est, omne quod
mouetur, ab alio mo-
ueri.

page.notes: Catchword "Quo-" at lower right, partly visible. Show-through from the reverse page is faint in the lower half and was excluded. The "s" beside "k" at the foot is a signature-like mark and was treated as furniture; "k s" is possibly a gathering signature, shown here only in the main text as printed. Ligature "Quo" with a raised macron in "Quòd" and "Quo-" is a printed form and kept as printed. Some words in lines 3 and 5 of the second paragraph ("sursum", "illa") are clear but the printed pencil-like spot near "mouentur" was ignored.
